whys.evidence: bun run audit:rin reports CD-20 bare node: stdlib imports (node:child_process, node:fs, node:os, node:path) at plugins/discipline-core/scripts/install-proof-ports.ts:1-4 without this entry; the Gate-5 review of rin record 261014-discipline-core-foundati required the install proof's process and filesystem effects behind injected ports (CD-18) with co-located tests (CD-23).

whyChain.rootCause: The install proof needs real filesystem and subprocess effects from the runtime, and CD-19/CD-21 place that dependency in one co-located wrapping port whose binding the static audit cannot distinguish from an unconfined import.

reason: The one adapter that reads files for the GitHub bot tooling, behind the TextFileReader and CanonicalPathResolver ports. Carried from the minutesarah-shop implementation into the rin plugin so every consumer receives one copy.

whys.why: Why does text-file-reader.ts import node:fs/promises?
whys.because: It implements the TextFileReader and CanonicalPathResolver ports, returning file text or a canonical path, or a file-unreadable failure
whys.evidence: plugins/rin/tools/github-apps/infrastructure/text-file-reader.ts exports readTextFile and resolveCanonicalPath against application/text-file-port.ts; nothing else in the package imports node:fs

whys.why: Why must the bot tooling read files at all?
whys.because: The identity configuration, the credential store, the app private keys and --body-file bodies all live on disk, and a body file is resolved to its real path before it is checked against the credential store
whys.evidence: identity-configuration.ts, file-credential-store.ts and application/read-body-file.ts take readTextFile, and read-body-file.ts takes resolveCanonicalPath, as dependencies

whys.why: Why do those callers not import node:fs themselves?
whys.because: They depend on the port types, and composition-root.ts injects the one implementation
whys.evidence: file-credential-store.test.ts, identity-configuration.test.ts and read-body-file.test.ts run against vi.fn<TextFileReader>() and vi.fn<CanonicalPathResolver>() fakes

whys.why: Why an authorised location rather than a carve-out?
whys.because: An adapter importing the runtime it wraps is permanent structure, not debt that should decay on touch
whys.evidence: plugins/discipline-core/rules/CD-19/README.md says to use authorised-location for the wrapping file

whys.why: Why only this file?
whys.because: Replacing the file system binding must touch one file, so only the adapter sees the node:fs surface
whys.evidence: CD-19 rule text: a dependency swap then touches one file and vendor types never leak inward

whyChain.rootCause: The GitHub bot tooling inverts file access behind the TextFileReader and CanonicalPathResolver ports, and this adapter is the one place those ports are implemented

whys.why: Why does rs256-signer.ts import node:crypto?

reason: The one adapter that reads the per-user environment for the GitHub bot tooling, behind the UserEnvironment port

whys.why: Why does user-environment.ts import node:os?
whys.because: It implements the UserEnvironment port, naming the home directory with homedir and reading one environment variable
whys.evidence: plugins/rin/tools/github-apps/infrastructure/user-environment.ts exports UserEnvironment and createProcessUserEnvironment

whys.why: Why must the bot tooling know the home directory at all?
whys.because: The app credentials live in one per-user store outside every repository, at ~/.config/rin-github-apps unless RIN_GITHUB_APPS_CREDENTIALS_DIR names another directory
whys.evidence: infrastructure/file-credential-store.ts locateUserStore builds the store directory from UserEnvironment

whys.why: Why is the store outside every repository rather than in the primary checkout as minutesarah had it?
whys.because: The tooling now ships in the rin plugin to many consumers, and one store means each private key exists once and is never inside a checkout that could commit it
whys.evidence: HailsTails/minutesarah-shop#10 handover: recommendation for the harness is one per-user store outside every repository with an environment-variable override

whys.why: Why does file-credential-store.ts not import node:os itself?
whys.because: It takes UserEnvironment as a dependency, so the store location is tested against a plain fake
whys.evidence: file-credential-store.test.ts locateUserStore cases run against an in-memory UserEnvironment

whys.why: Why an authorised location rather than a carve-out?
whys.because: An adapter importing the runtime it wraps is permanent structure, not debt that should decay on touch, and only this file sees the node:os surface
whys.evidence: plugins/discipline-core/rules/CD-19/README.md says to use an authorised location for the wrapping file
